You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

This is a public goods game with negative externalities: keeping a token privately gives me +1 but costs each of the 3 others 0.3 points, while giving a token to the group only pays me 0.3 with no effect on others, so socially the private-keeping option creates a net externality loss even though it's individually better for me.

Running the numbers: full defection by everyone nets each person just 2 points, while full cooperation nets each person 6 points, so mutual cooperation is clearly superior even though individual incentives push toward keeping tokens. With 10 rounds and 4 players, I'm thinking about whether to open with cooperation and use a conditional strategy, weighing the risk that if I contribute everything and others defect, I end up worse off than if I'd also kept my tokens.

I'll start round 1 by contributing all 20 tokens to the group fund as a cooperative signal, then adjust my strategy based on how others behave.
